name: Guul Draz Vampire
oracle_text: As long as an opponent has 10 or less life, this creature gets +2/+1 and has intimidate. (It can't be blocked except by artifact creatures and/or creatures that share a color with it.)
blocked_sentences: As long as an opponent has 10 or less life, this creature gets +2/+1 and has intimidate. (It can't be blocked except by artifact creatures and/or creatures that share a color with it.)

Scope (updated): two of the three blockers on this card's ONE printed line have now shipped. `static_condition` gave the "as long as" tree, and `intimidate` is `Keyword.INTIMIDATE`, compared on derived colors in `combat.can_block` -- so `"keywords": ["intimidate"]` and a conditional `buff` with `affects.self_only` are both expressible today. The card is blocked on exactly one thing: the condition has no leaf that can ask about ONE opponent's life total.

needs.what: The static `condition` tree itself has SHIPPED (see `tests/unit/test_static_condition.py`): a static may now carry `all`/`any`/`not`/`exists`/`is_your_turn`/`cmp` over `{"const": n}` and `{"count": filter}`, and the count filter may name a zone. What is still missing for this card is a *leaf* for that tree to read, and it is the leaf named below, not the tree. Concretely: a static condition can express the SHAPE of "as long as an opponent has 10 or less life" today, but a static value is `const` or `count` only -- there is no `life_of` leaf, and the one in the `if`-effect language would be wrong here anyway because it SUMS. What this card needs is a per-opponent life leaf readable from a static condition: `min_life_of` over a multi-player spec, or the general `{"any_player": {"players": "each_opponent", "condition": {...}}}` form -- so that "an opponent has 10 or less life" is a question about SOME ONE opponent. the existential over individual opponents already specified in the Vampire Lacerator gap record -- `min_life_of` / `max_life_of` over a multi-player spec, or the general `{"any_player": {"players": "each_opponent", "condition": {...}}}` condition form -- so that "an opponent has 10 or less life" is a question about SOME ONE opponent. Needed here in whatever condition language the `static_condition` item above ends up with, not only in the `if`-effect language
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `life_of` is the only way to read a life total and it SUMS over its player spec (`engine/effects/values.py:102-104` does `sum(ctx.state.players[p].life for p in pids)`), while `"opponent"` and `"each_opponent"` are the same thing -- `select_players` returns `ctx.opponents()` for both. So even granting the `static_condition` item above, `{"cmp": "<=", "left": {"life_of": "opponent"}, "right": {"const": 10}}` would read "my opponents' COMBINED life is 10 or less". In a duel that matches the printed card; in a pod it is a different card, and the wrong way round -- three opponents at 4 life each sum to 12, so this creature would stay a 1/1 against a table that is nearly dead. This engine is multiplayer and this repo is Commander-first, so that is a divergence rather than a rounding error. `min`/`max` exist as value expressions but take a literal list of value expressions, and no player spec enumerates opponents one at a time to feed them
